text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT ALERT: elevated p95/p99 tail latency and streaming stalls detected in shared-gpu pool 'pool-west-2a'. Automated SLO monitor tripped (latency_slo_streaming).

incident-bot: Summary metrics snapshot:
```
p95=420ms (baseline 120ms)
p99=1.8s (baseline 400ms)
streaming_stalls/sec=28 (norm <2)
agg_error_rate=0.4%
affected_tenants=~12 (heavy tail)
```

sarah: Paging oncall. I'm oncall now, taking lead. :wave: Anyone from infra nearby?

raj: I'm here, looking. Noted heavy IO wait on GPUs in that pool. Checking cgroup stats.

emily: I'll pull recent routing history and model fallbacks. Could be a noisy-tenant causing KV cache thrash.

mike: Support-bot flagged two customers reporting streaming stalls. Ticket ids: 8912, 8913. @support-bot can you paste customer impact details?

support-bot: Customer 8912: intermittent stalls on long chat sessions, 20% of sessions saw retries. Customer 8913: increase in 502s during stalls. Both on region us-west-2.

raj: Running quick topo: `ssh infra-pool-west-2a` then `sudo cgget -r memory.usage_in_bytes` for top pods. I see tenants A and D with sustained high memory+writeback. Also high `nvme0n1` iowait.

emily: Routing shows recent autoscale bumped more pods for tenant A at 16:03 UTC then we saw latency rise. Could be shard imbalance.

sarah: Ok hypotheses: noisy tenant causing IO / cgroup interference -> KV cache thrash -> streaming stalls and p99 tail. Mitigations to try: 1) move top noisy tenants to dedicated pool (if capacity), 2) temporarily lower concurrency for heavy tenants, 3) adjust cgroup io.weight for offending containers, 4) fallback to smaller model shard with lower IO. Which is fastest?

raj: Fastest: reduce concurrency / impose throughput cap on noisy tenants via QoS (we can push a quick QoS update). We can also evict the largest tenants to a quarantine pool if capacity exists.

mike: I can run a temporary throttle policy via `infra-cli tenant-throttle --tenant A --max-concurrent 4 --reason "incident 3055554321"` — should be near-instant, rolls back manually.

emily: Meanwhile I'll prepare a canary reroute for new requests to use dedicated-pool-small (if approved), and set model fallback for streaming to 1.2B quantized variant to reduce KV/IO. That needs ~2-3 min to propagate.

sarah: Do it. mike, please apply throttle. Raj, can you check if we have capacity in dedicated pools for a handful of tenants?

raj: Checking capacity: dedicated-pool-small has 6 free slots, dedicated-pool-medium has 1. So we can move up to 6 pods quickly. Which tenants?

mike: Throttle applied for tenant A and D: `--max-concurrent 4` on both. Confirming: API shows active concurrency dropped from 18->4 for each.

emily: Initiating model fallback for streaming route: set `streaming.model_preference = [small-quantized, baseline-v2]` in route config and deploy. Deploy id: dep-2026-03-15-1.

raj: Moving tenant A's hottest replica to dedicated-pool-small now. `kubectl cordon/evict` sequence done; new pod in dedicated pool is healthy. Latency for that tenant dropped immediately to p95=160ms.

sarah: Good. Any change in aggregated metrics?

incident-bot: Updated metrics (2m post-mitigation):
```
p95=180ms
p99=650ms
streaming_stalls/sec=6
```

sarah: That's promising but p99 still high. Anyone see residual IO hotspots?

raj: There's still tail IO from tenant G (smaller but high writeback patterns). Their writeback is causing nvme queue backlog. I can lower their cgroup `io.weight` from 1000 -> 200 to deprioritize.

mike: Fine with that. Doing `cgset -r blkio.weight=200 <cgid>` now.

infra-sre: Note: lowering io.weight can increase latency for that tenant; coordinate with support if impacted customers are external.

support-bot: Customer 8920 (tenant G) small internal partner, low SLA. No immediate external-ticket present.

raj: io.weight change applied. Observing nvme0 queue depth decreasing, iowait down 40%.

incident-bot: Updated metrics (5m):
```
p95=150ms
p99=430ms
streaming_stalls/sec=1.2
```

emily: Model fallback seems to reduce KV cache miss pressure as well. Nice.

sarah: Great. Let's move to stabilization plan and postmortem actions. Immediate items: 1) Keep throttle for A/D for 30 minutes; 2) Keep tenant A on dedicated pool until follow-up; 3) Revert cgroup io.weight after load normalizes; 4) Run root-cause data collection for top 12 tenants (traces, KV cache evictions, writeback stats).

mike: I'll schedule revert for throttles at +30m unless we see regression. I'll annotate throttle with `expires=now+30m`.

raj: I'll take the data collection: running `iostat -x 1 30`, `nvme top`, `cgget` snapshots, and dump `runtime-kv` hit/miss logs for last hour. Uploading to /tmp/incident-3055554321.tar.gz (link: https://internal.storage/incident-3055554321.tar.gz).

support-bot: Notifying account managers for the two customers impacted. Draft message: "We're investigating streaming stalls in us-west-2; mitigation in place; we'll follow up." Want me to send now?

sarah: Send now with ETA 1h, mention we've reduced stalls and are continuing investigation.

support-bot: Sent.

emily: Postmortem action candidates: - Add automatic tenant isolation when p99 crossing with IO signal - Add adaptive io.weight policy based on long-running writeback - Improve routing to avoid shard concentration after autoscale events - Add streaming-specific SLO alert for sustained stalls > 5/sec

sarah: +1 on all. Also we should schedule a follow-up meeting with runtime and infra to discuss capacity knobs. I'll create an incident channel and assign owners in the postmortem doc.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Slack thread will be archived after P0 review.

mike: Throttles set to auto-expire in 30m. I'll remain available.

raj: Data upload completed and looks complete. Happy to hand off to oncall for long-term follow-up.

sarah: Thanks team. Handoff summary: mitigations applied (throttle A/D, moved A to dedicated, io.weight reduce for G, model fallbacks). Customer comms sent. Monitoring shows p99 back under threshold but remain on watch. Handoff to follow-up oncall: @emily please take next shift for postmortem actions.

emily: Taking follow-up. I'll collect logs and start the RCA doc.

mike: Ping me if any regressions, will jump back in. :thumbsup:
